We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner and the Respondents IBEUL/JSWEL and SEL/JPPL and perused the material on record. The Petitioner has 6. The Petitioner has submitted that as per the directions of the Commission in the order dated 24.1.2020 in Petition No. 394/MP/2019, the Petitioner has lodged claims in the CIRP/ liquidation proceedings against Respondent Nos. 1 and 2 before NCLT for the recovery of 23. We have considered the submissions of the parties. The principal contention of the Petitioner is that despite having pursued its claims before the Resolution Professional and the Liquidator in terms of the directions by this Commission in its order dated 24.1.2020 in Petition No.394/MP/2019, it has not been able to recover the outstanding transmission charges and relinquishment charges in full. The Petitioner has, therefore, prayed that the Commission may issue appropriate directions so as to ensure recovery of the outstanding Yearly Transmission Charges and to protect the financial integrity of the PoC mechanism. _Provided further that the Adjudicating Authority may, on an application made by the resolution professional, with the approval of the committee of creditors, by a vote of not less than sixty-six per cent. of the voting share, in such form and manner, and subject to such conditions as may be specified, first approve the implementation of the resolution plan and thereafter approve the manner of distribution provided therein within a period of thirty days from the date of approval of implementation of such resolution plan.”_ 27. Likewise, in respect of SEL, the Petitioner's claim stood subject to the liquidation 31. The Petitioner, relying upon the case of Adyah Solar Energy Pvt. Ltd. v. KER and Ors., has contended that the doctrine of _quantum meruit_ is applicable to the instant case. The Petitioner has contended that it would result in unjust enrichment if JSWEL and JPPL, who acquired the relevant assets/companies under the IBC processes, were permitted to retain the operational and commercial fruits of those assets without contribution in respect of transmission charges and relinquishment. We are unable to accept this contention of the Petitioner. The principle of _quantum meruit_ , being an equitable doctrine, cannot be invoked to circumvent the statutory scheme of the IBC or to revive claims which have attained finality under the IBC. In the present case, the Petitioner's claims towards transmission charges and relinquishment charges were admittedly lodged before the Resolution Professional/ Liquidator pursuant to the directions of this Commission and were thereafter dealt with in the insolvency/liquidation proceedings. The rights and liabilities of the stakeholders consequently came to be governed by the approved Resolution Plan in terms of Section 31 of the IBC and the waterfall mechanism under Section 53 of the IBC. We are of the view that once the claims have been subjected to the statutory framework of the IBC and the proceedings have attained finality, the equitable doctrine of _quantum meruit_ cannot be invoked to confer upon the Petitioner a right of recovery beyond what is permissible under the IBC. **_“27._** _In view thereof, we have pursued the documents annexed to the Petition and have heard the submissions made by the Petitioners and pass the following order: -_ _(c) All proceedings and/or suits and/ or appeals now pending by or against the Transferor Companies shall be continued by or against the Transferee Company; however, if any suit, writ petition, investigation appeal, criminal or other proceedings of whatsoever nature is pending against the petitioner Companies or entities associated with petitioner companies, their directors, shareholders, employees etc., the same shall not abate, be discontinued or be in any way prejudicially affected by reason of the transfer of business of the Transferor Company or because of anything contained in the scheme, but the proceeding shall continue, prosecuted and enforced by or against the Transferee Company/Transferor Company entities etc. in the same manner and to the same extent as it would or might have been continued, prosecuted and enforced by or against the Transferor Companies and their associated entities, directors, shareholders, employees etc. as if the Scheme had not been made._ _Respondent-CTUIL that the claim of erstwhile PGCIL which was the subject matter of the petition before the Commission and also form the subject matter of this appeal, stand extinguished and no longer survive. Therefore, the said appeal has become infructuous and is hereby dismissed.”_ 43. To the extent the Petitioner was aggrieved by the treatment of its claims in the insolvency or liquidation proceedings, or by the orders passed by NCLT, the remedy, if any, lay under the provisions of the IBC. The present proceedings cannot be invoked as an indirect means of obtaining relief inconsistent with, or beyond the statutory framework governing insolvency and liquidation. This Commission cannot, in exercise of its regulatory jurisdiction, revisit or modify the orders passed under the IBC. 45. In view of the foregoing discussion, we are of the considered view that the Petitioner's claims have already been dealt with in accordance with the provisions of the IBC and the legal consequences flowing therefrom have attained finality. Neither the Act nor any of the Regulations confer any power upon this Commission to direct recovery of the unrecovered transmission charges and relinquishment charges in matters which have already been decided under the IBC 2016.
